BookingRules.capacityHelp: How many people can book a new class. You can still change it on each class.
BookingRules.autoApproveHelp: On: a booking is confirmed at once, with no waiting. Off: each booking is a request that someone on staff approves, and you set how long it waits for an answer.
BookingRules.approvalWaitLabel: Time to answer a booking request
BookingRules.approvalWaitHelp: If nobody on staff answers a request within this time, it is cancelled, the visit goes back to the member and the place goes to the next person on the waitlist. “No limit”: the request waits for an answer until the class starts. This is not when bookings open: that is “Bookings open”.
BookingRules.approvalWaitClassHelp: If nobody on staff approves a request within this time, it is cancelled automatically and the place goes to the next person on the waitlist. “No limit”: the request waits for an answer until the class starts.
BookingRules.bookingWindowHelp: The earliest a member can book: this many days before the class. Bookings stay open until the class starts. With “No limit” a class can be booked as soon as it is on the schedule. A subscription package can set its own.
BookingRules.lateCancellationLabel: Late cancellation (how long before the class)
BookingRules.lateCancellationHelp: A member who cancels later than this still uses the visit, as if they came. Cancelling earlier gives the visit back. With “No limit” cancelling is always free. A subscription package can set its own, in whole hours.
BookingRules.answerTimeHelp: After this the request is cancelled automatically.

Ui.perseveranceHelpWhat: How closely you followed the programme on your last 7 training days (rest days do not count). Every exercise you skipped, or did with different weight or reps from what the WOD said, lowers it, by as much as you strayed.
Ui.perseveranceHelpHow: Do the exercises as they are written. If you have logged no changes, the score is 100%.
Ui.perseveranceHelpWhy: Your coach's programme is built to progress step by step. The closer you stay to it, the better it works.
Ui.scoreLevelTooltip: Points from everything you do, and the level they reach
Ui.scoreLevelHelpWhat: The experience points (XP) you earn from what you do: a workout +{workouts}, a PR +{prs}, a week on your weekly goal +{weeks}, a challenge you complete +{challenges}.
Ui.scoreLevelHelpHow: Train, set PRs, reach your weekly goal and finish challenges. Each level takes a little more XP than the one before.
Ui.scoreLevelHelpWhy: Every workout counts towards something you can see, even while the next PR is still a while away.
Ui.scoreStrengthTooltip: How much your estimated 1RM went up in the last 8 weeks
Ui.scoreStrengthHelpWhat: How much the estimated one-rep max of your weight PRs went up on average in the last 8 weeks, compared with your best before them. Each lift weighs the same, light or heavy.
Ui.scoreStrengthHelpHow: Log your PRs with weight and reps. Every new PR raises the estimate, even more reps at the same weight.
Ui.scoreStrengthHelpWhy: You see the work paying off between one-rep records, not only on the day you beat one.

Ui.scoreNextMilestoneHelpHow: Do what the card says. Once you earn the badge, the card shows the next one.
Ui.scoreNextMilestoneHelpWhy: A close, concrete goal is easier to reach than a distant one.

Ui.classTimerOnScreenHelp: Show this class’s timer, leaderboard or WOD on one of the box’s screens for today.
Ui.classTimerOpenHereHelp: When this device is the room’s screen.
Ui.classTimerSoundHelp: Beeps on this device in the last 3 seconds and at every phase change. It does not change the wall screen’s sound.
Ui.classTimerClockHelp: “—” means there is no time yet. Time reads minutes:seconds; when it counts down, it shows what is left. “Next” is the part that follows.
Ui.classTimerCountdownHelp: How many seconds the screen counts down before the start, so athletes can get in place.
Ui.classTimerStartHelp: Starts the clock on every screen after the countdown.
Ui.classTimerPauseHelp: Stops the clock on every screen. The time is kept.
Ui.classTimerResumeHelp: Carries on where it stopped, after a 3-second countdown.
Ui.classTimerBackHelp: Goes to the previous part and starts it from the beginning.
Ui.classTimerRestartHelp: This is the first part, so it starts again from the beginning.
Ui.classTimerNextHelp: Ends the current part and starts the next one at once.
Ui.classTimerCompleteHelp: This is the last part, so the timer ends and the screens show “Time!”.
Ui.classTimerAdjustHelp: Takes 30 seconds off or adds 30 seconds to the current part, for everyone.
Ui.classTimerFinishHelp: Ends the timer now. The screens show “Time!”.
Ui.classTimerResetHelp: Clears the clock on every screen and goes back to “Ready”.
Ui.classTimerResetConfirmBody: The clock clears on every screen in the room and goes back to “Ready”.
Ui.classTimerNoTimedWorkout: This class has no timed workout.
Ui.classTimerJumpHelp: Tap a part to go straight to it.
Ui.timerPresetHelp_tabata: Tabata: 20 seconds of work, 10 of rest, 8 rounds (4 minutes).
Ui.timerPresetHelp_emom10: EMOM (Every Minute On the Minute): at the start of every minute you do the work and rest for what is left. 10 rounds.
Ui.timerPresetHelp_e2mom20: E2MOM: like EMOM, but every 2 minutes. 10 rounds, 20 minutes.
Ui.timerPresetHelp_amrap12: AMRAP (As Many Rounds As Possible): as many rounds as you can in 12 minutes.
Ui.timerPresetHelp_forTime12: For Time: finish as fast as you can. Time cap 12: the clock stops at 12 minutes.
Ui.timerPresetHelp_deathBy: Death By: an EMOM where you add one rep every minute until you can’t keep up.
Ui.timerPresetHelp_stopwatch: Stopwatch: counts up with no limit until you stop it.

WorkoutAssistant.title: Workout assistant
WorkoutAssistant.intro: Write the workout like you would on the whiteboard. The assistant turns it into structured data and points out anything unclear.
WorkoutAssistant.analyzingHint: This usually takes a few seconds. Your text is saved.
WorkoutAssistant.stale: You changed the text since the last check. Check again to update the results.
WorkoutAssistant.exampleWorkout:
Murph prep
Warm-up: 400m run, then 2 rounds of 10 air squats
For time, cap 25 min:
5 rounds
10 pull-ups
20 push-ups
30 air squats
Strength:
Back squat 5x5 @ 100 kg, rest 2 min
WorkoutAssistant.tipSetsReps: Write sets × reps @ load, e.g. 5x5 @ 100 kg.
WorkoutAssistant.tipBlocks: Name each block: Warm-up, Strength, WOD.
WorkoutAssistant.tipTimers: State timers: AMRAP 12, EMOM 10, For time cap 20.
WorkoutAssistant.allClear: Everything is clear. You can publish.
WorkoutAssistant.rejectedRequired: rejected, required: publishing is blocked until you add it
WorkoutAssistant.rejectOptionalHint: Reject leaves this field empty. The workout can still be published.
WorkoutAssistant.rejectRequiredHint: This field is required. Rejecting it empties the field and blocks publishing until you add a value.
WorkoutAssistant.invalidTyped: That value doesn’t fit this field. Check the format and try again.
WorkoutAssistant.alsoInText: Also add this line to the text:
WorkoutAssistant.noBlocks: No training blocks found yet. Add exercises, one per line.

why.difficulty: Athletes pick workouts faster when they know the level.
why.estimated_duration_seconds: A duration helps you plan classes and helps athletes plan their day.
why.equipment: Listing equipment lets athletes set up before they start.
why.description: A short goal or intent keeps everyone focused.
why.generic: Adding this makes the workout more complete.

codes.missing_title: Your workout needs a title. Type one in the Title field, e.g. “Murph prep”.
codes.missing_type: Choose a workout type so the workout lands in the right library.
codes.missing_section_name: Give this block a name, e.g. “Warm-up” or “Strength”.
codes.missing_exercise_name: This line has numbers but no movement. Write which exercise it is.
codes.invalid_value: “{value}” isn’t valid here. Enter a correct value or reject it to leave it out.
codes.invalid_timer: The {format} timer is missing: {missing}. Add it to the text, e.g. “every 1 min for 10 min”.
codes.unknown_format: “{value}” isn’t a timer format we know. Use one like AMRAP, EMOM or For time.
codes.generic: The assistant found something to check here.

errors.notConfigured: The assistant isn’t set up on this server yet. You can still publish the text as it is.
errors.unavailable: The assistant is busy or offline. Try again in a moment. Your text is saved.
errors.quotaExhausted: The assistant has run out of credits. Ask the app administrator to top up the AI account. Your text is saved and you can still publish it as it is.
errors.textRequired: Write the workout first, then check it.
errors.textTooLong: This text is too long to check at once. Split it into separate workouts.

WorkoutAssistant.blockingTitle: Can’t publish yet. Fix these first:
WorkoutAssistant.titlePlaceholder: Leave empty to let the assistant propose one

WorkoutAssistant.publishFailed: Publishing failed. Your draft is saved. Try again.
WorkoutAssistant.rejectTextHint: Reject keeps your text as written.

WorkoutAssistant.rejectAssumptionHint: Reject clears this value; the coach's text stays as written.

about.sternocleidomastoid: Turns and bends the head and helps when you breathe hard.
about.scalenes: Tilt the neck to the side and lift the upper ribs as you breathe in.
about.splenius: Extends and turns the head and holds it up.
about.deltoid: Lifts the arm forward, to the side and back; it shapes the shoulder.
about.rotator-cuff: Four small muscles that keep the shoulder centred and rotate the arm.
about.pectoralis-major: Brings the arm across the body and pushes forward, as in a push-up.
about.pectoralis-minor: Pulls the shoulder blade forward and down.
about.serratus-anterior: Holds the shoulder blade against the ribs and turns it upward overhead.
about.trapezius: Lifts, squeezes and lowers the shoulder blades and supports the neck.
about.rhomboids: Squeeze the shoulder blades together, as in a row.
about.levator-scapulae: Lifts the shoulder blade and tilts the neck.
about.latissimus-dorsi: Pulls the arm down and back, as in a pull-up; the widest back muscle.
about.teres-major: Helps the lats pull the arm down and turn it inward.
about.erector-spinae: Straightens the spine and holds it upright when you lift or hinge.
about.multifidus: Small deep muscles that steady each vertebra.
about.quadratus-lumborum: Bends the trunk to the side and steadies the pelvis and lower back.
about.biceps-brachii: Bends the elbow and turns the palm up.
about.brachialis: The main elbow flexor, whichever way the palm faces.
about.triceps-brachii: Straightens the elbow, as in a press or a push-up.
about.brachioradialis: Bends the elbow with the thumb up, as in a hammer curl.
about.forearm-flexors: Bend the wrist and fingers and give you grip.
about.forearm-extensors: Straighten the wrist and fingers and balance the grip.
about.rectus-abdominis: Bends the trunk forward and braces the front of the core.
about.obliques: Twist and side-bend the trunk and resist rotation.
about.transversus-abdominis: The deepest abdominal muscle; it tightens the waist like a belt.
about.diaphragm: The main breathing muscle; it also helps brace the trunk under load.
about.glutes: Extend and open the hip and keep the pelvis level; key in squats and jumps.
about.hip-flexors: Lift the knee towards the chest and bend the trunk at the hip.
about.hip-rotators: Turn the thigh outward and keep the hip stable.
about.quadriceps: Straighten the knee; they drive squats, lunges and jumps.
about.hamstrings: Bend the knee and extend the hip, as in a deadlift.
about.adductors: Bring the legs together and help the hip in deep squats.
about.calves: Lift the heel; they push off when you run and jump.
about.tibialis-anterior: Lifts the toes and controls the foot as it lands.
about.fibularis: Turns the sole outward and steadies the ankle.

totals.what: How much you trained in the chosen period: completed sessions, their minutes and how many different workouts they were.
totals.how: Every completed workout of the period, from the sources you picked, counts once. Minutes are each workout's recorded duration; a workout you repeated counts once among the different workouts.
totals.change: Each workout you finish adds to the numbers. A shorter period or fewer sources lowers them.

weekly.what: Your training per calendar week, as sessions or minutes.
weekly.how: Completed workouts go into the week they were finished in, Monday first. Each bar is one week of the period; a week without training stays empty.
weekly.change: A bar grows with every workout you finish that week. Switching between sessions and minutes changes only what the bars show.

consistency.what: How regularly you train: the weeks of the period that reached your weekly target (or, without a target, had any training), the days you trained and your streak.
consistency.how: Each column is a week and each square a day, darker with more sessions. A week counts when its sessions reach your weekly target; the percentage is those weeks out of all weeks of the period.
consistency.change: It rises with every week you reach your target and falls when a week stays below it. A new weekly target changes which weeks count.

scoreHistory.what: How your score moved in the sections you logged more than once.
scoreHistory.how: Every score of the same section of the same workout, from any source, makes one line, oldest to newest. The figure next to it is your latest score.
scoreHistory.change: Each new score in that section adds a point to its line.

bySource.what: Where the sessions of the period came from: your box, training on your own or a device.
bySource.how: Completed sessions are counted per source; each bar is that source's share of all of them.
bySource.change: Training more with one source makes its share grow; the shares always add up to the whole.

prTimeline.what: The personal records you beat in the period, month by month.
prTimeline.how: Each entry is a new record on the day you set it, with how much it improved on the one before; a first record has nothing to compare with.
prTimeline.change: A new entry appears every time you beat a record. A shorter period hides older ones; nothing is deleted.

depthCoverage.what: Which muscles your training of the period worked most and least, and the balance of push and pull and of the front and back of the thigh.
depthCoverage.how: The sets of each exercise the app recognises count for the muscles it trains, per week of the period. The levels compare those weekly sets; exercises it does not recognise are left out.
depthCoverage.change: A muscle rises when you add sets for it. More recognised exercises in your log make the picture more complete.

depthQualities.what: Which of the ten fitness qualities, from endurance and strength to balance and accuracy, your training of the period worked.
depthQualities.how: The sets of each recognised exercise count for the qualities it trains. The shape compares the qualities with each other: the most trained one sets the outer edge.
depthQualities.change: Training a quality more pushes it outwards. The shape shows the balance between qualities, not a level.

depthLoad.what: How demanding this week was compared with your usual week.
depthLoad.how: A session's load is its RPE (1–10) times its minutes; sessions without RPE or duration do not count. The last 7 days are compared with your weekly average of the last 28.
depthLoad.change: It rises when this week is harder than usual and falls when it is lighter. It is an indicator, not medical advice.

SiteInfo.whatIsAnswer: Palee is a training platform for boxes, coaches and athletes. It brings class scheduling and booking, personalised programming, live workout execution, coaching conversations and progress tracking into one app.
SiteInfo.whoForAnswer: Box owners and staff who run classes, coaches who program for athletes, and members who book classes and log their training.
SiteInfo.offlineAnswer: Yes. A workout keeps running without a connection: check-offs are saved on the device and sync when the connection returns.
SiteInfo.adsAnswer: No. Palee shows no ads and does not track members for advertising. Training progress belongs to the athlete.
SiteInfo.languagesAnswer: English, Greek, Arabic, Russian, German, Spanish, Portuguese, Hebrew, Italian, Bulgarian, Dutch and French.
SiteInfo.twoSidesQuestion: Is Palee for boxes or for individual people?
SiteInfo.twoSidesAnswer: Both. Palee has two sides in one app: a business side where boxes, studios and independent coaches run classes, clients, coaching and finance, and a social side where anyone, with or without a box, keeps a training journal, joins clubs, finds training partners and goes to events.
SiteInfo.twoSidesSummary: Palee has two sides in one app: a business side where boxes (gyms, studios) and independent coaches run classes, members, coaching and finance, and a social side where anyone, with or without a box, keeps a training journal, joins clubs, finds training partners and goes to events.
SiteInfo.eventsQuestion: Can I organise events with Palee?
SiteInfo.eventsAnswer: Yes. Boxes, coaches, clubs and individual organisers can publish events such as open WODs, bootcamps, runs and competitions, with capacity, waitlist, guest passes, co-hosts and an organiser console for management, finances and analytics. Nearby events appear in Around me.
SiteInfo.socialSummary: A feed of your clubs and the people you follow, club channels, posts with photos and workouts, and Around me to discover nearby events, open clubs and boxes on a map.
SiteInfo.partnersSummary: Find a training partner among verified adults near you, matched only if you both want to, and pick a check-in buddy who hears from you only when you ask for help.
SiteInfo.eventsSummary: Open WODs, bootcamps, runs and competitions with RSVPs, capacity, waitlist, guest passes, co-hosting and an organiser console for management, finances and analytics.
SiteInfo.boxSummary: Book classes and appointments, check in with a rotating QR code, a Wallet pass or NFC, see today's workout, follow your subscription packages and pay, all from one Box tab.
SiteInfo.trainingSummary: Run any workout with a step-synchronised timer, scaling options, per-exercise notes, injury warnings and offline check-offs, or log a score in seconds, even by voice.
SiteInfo.journalSummary: Every workout, PR, note and rating in one journal that belongs to the athlete and follows them across boxes and coaches, private by default with a clear visibility ladder.
SiteInfo.bodySummary: Body measurements and progress photos with a pose guide and compare slider, plus water, sleep, meals, mood and cravings, with health-safe defaults such as showing weight as a trend only.
SiteInfo.progressSummary: Consistency, strength, benchmarks, muscle coverage on a 3D anatomy atlas, the ten fitness qualities, training load and insights such as sleep versus performance.
SiteInfo.businessSummary: Class schedules and recurring classes, appointments, check-in desk, workout library with goals, challenges, community moderation, inventory, cleaning log, reviews and reports.
SiteInfo.coachingSummary: Programs, reply and form-review queues, nutrition plans, coach notes, PT squads and session packages; independent coaches get their own lighter console and a team club.
SiteInfo.financeSummary: Subscription packages and seasons, promotions, member billing, invoices and refunds, corporate clients, reconciliation and accounting exports.
SiteInfo.growthSummary: A public box page, trial classes the owner controls, member referrals with rewards and open events bring new clients while the relationship stays with the box.
SiteInfo.branchesSummary: Staff roles and permissions scoped to branches, a branch filter across finance, coaching and statistics, and one-step creation of classes or subscription packages for several branches.
SiteInfo.devicesSummary: An installable web app that works offline, native iOS and Android builds, Garmin, Apple Health and Health Connect, home-screen widgets, calendar feeds and push notifications.
SiteInfo.privacySummary: No ads, private-by-default data, report and block tools, data export, each box in its own time zone, and the whole app in twelve languages.

privacy.intro: This policy explains what personal data Palee keeps when you use the app, why, who else processes it, how long it is kept and what you can do about it.
privacy.controllerBody: {controller}, {address}, is responsible for your data in Palee (the controller). Contact: {contact}.
privacy.boxRoleBody: When you train at a box that uses Palee, the box decides about its own records of you (membership, bookings, payments, documents you sign) and Palee processes them on its behalf. For those records you can also contact the box.
privacy.dataAccount: Account: your name, @handle, email, password (stored only as a hash), language and settings.
privacy.dataProfile: Profile: your photo, bio, the boxes you belong to and the people you follow.
privacy.dataBookings: Bookings and attendance: the classes you book, check-ins and waiting lists.
privacy.dataTraining: Training: your journal, workouts, results and personal records.
privacy.dataWellness: Wellness and body: what you enter yourself, such as sleep, mood, weight, measurements and body photos.
privacy.dataFoodShares: Foods you share: only if you choose it for an own food with a barcode, the product (barcode, name, brand, portion and nutrition per 100 g, without your name or your meals) becomes available to everyone on Palee and is sent to Open Food Facts under the ODbL licence. We keep internally who shared it and when, only to deal with abuse; this is erased with your account.
privacy.dataHealth: Health and device data: only if you connect Health Connect, Apple Health or Garmin, the workouts and readings you allow (such as heart rate).
privacy.dataMessages: Messages and community: what you write in chats, posts and comments.
privacy.dataPayments: Payments: what you pay a box, how, and a card's brand and last four digits. Full card numbers go only to the payment provider.
privacy.dataDocuments: Documents: receipts and invoices for your payments, and documents you sign with a box (such as the date of a health certificate).
privacy.dataLocation: Location: the area you choose to see what is near you and the places you search for. Palee does not track your location in the background.
privacy.dataPartners: Training partners: if you use them, your training partner profile, your swipes, matches and messages, how you were verified and the reports you make. The details are in “Training partners” below.
privacy.dataTechnical: Technical: device and notification identifiers, sign-in sessions and security logs.
privacy.dataNotCollected: Palee does not ask for your date of birth, does not sell your data and does not use it for advertising.
privacy.purposeContract: To provide the app you signed up for: your account, bookings, training, messages and payments (performance of our contract with you).
privacy.purposeLegal: To keep the business records the law requires, such as receipts and invoices (legal obligation).
privacy.purposeConsent: Health and device data, and optional features such as AI help, only with your consent, which you can withdraw at any time.
privacy.purposeSecurity: To keep Palee safe and working, for example to prevent abuse and fix errors (legitimate interest).
privacy.healthBody: If you connect Health Connect, Apple Health or Garmin, Palee reads only the data types you allow, to show your workouts and progress in your journal. This data is never sold or used for advertising, and your box sees it only if you choose to share it. You can disconnect a device at any time from your devices page, and delete what was imported from your journal.
privacy.partnersIntro: Training partners is optional and only for people aged 18 or older. When you use it, Palee processes the following, to run the feature you asked for and to keep it safe.
privacy.partnersProfile: Your training partner profile: your photo, name, level, training times, goals, disciplines and a short line of your own, shown only to other verified people in training partners. Your card also shows how you were verified and, while you are a member, your box's name, which you can hide. Your gender is optional, is used only to respect gender preferences and is never shown.
privacy.partnersDistance: Distance: only an approximate step (2, 5, 10 or 25 km) between the centre of your main neighbourhood and the other person's. Palee never uses your live location for this.
privacy.partnersVerification: Verification, once per account: either an active membership at a box, or an active package with an independent coach, on Palee (we record which one verified you), or two people who vouch for you plus a check by the Palee team. We keep who vouched for you and the outcome.
privacy.partnersPhone: Mobile number (only when two people vouch for you): stored encrypted, one number per account, and used only to send you an SMS code and to stop one person from verifying several accounts. Nobody else sees it; the Palee team sees only part of it.
privacy.partnersSelfie: Selfie with a code (only when two people vouch for you): a photo of you holding a 4-digit code written on paper. Only a member of the Palee team sees it, to compare it with your profile photo. There is no face recognition and no automatic decision: a person decides. The photo is deleted as soon as the decision is taken, and at the latest 7 days after you upload it; only the outcome is kept. If you disagree with the decision, you can ask for a second review by writing to {contact}.
privacy.partnersConsent: Consent: the phone and selfie check starts only after you give your consent in the app. You can withdraw it at any time by withdrawing your verification request: your number, the selfie and your open requests to sponsors are deleted. You can also hide yourself from training partners in your settings, or delete your account.
privacy.partnersReports: Reports: reports in training partners are reviewed by the Palee team, not by your box. If an account is suspended after reports, the people who vouched for it are told and cannot vouch for anyone for 60 days.
privacy.recipientsIntro: These services process personal data on Palee's behalf, only for the purpose shown.
privacy.purposeSms: Sending SMS codes to check a mobile number (training partners)
privacy.purposeAi: AI features you choose to use, such as reading a workout from a photo
privacy.purposeNetwork: Delivering the site securely and protecting it from attacks
privacy.purposeFiscalSigning: Signing receipts as tax law requires
privacy.purposeTaxAuthority: Reporting receipts and invoices to the Greek tax authority (a public authority, not a processor)
privacy.separateControllerBody: {name}: if you connect your Garmin account, Garmin decides about its own part under its own privacy policy, and Palee about the data it receives.
privacy.transfersBody: Some of these services may process data outside the European Economic Area, for example in the United States. Such transfers rely on the EU–US Data Privacy Framework or on the European Commission's standard contractual clauses. [To be confirmed for each service.]
privacy.retentionAccount: Your account: until you delete it. When you ask, it is deleted after 7 days, and until then you can undo it.
privacy.retentionBox: A box's records of you, including signed documents and their certificates: while you are its member, and for 5 years after the box is deleted from Palee.
privacy.retentionFiscal: Receipts and invoices: as long as tax law requires, even after your account is deleted.
privacy.retentionExport: Your data file: 7 days after it is ready.
privacy.retentionPartners: Training partners: your profile, matches, messages and verification until you delete your account; the selfie until the decision, and at most 7 days after upload; SMS codes for at most one day.
privacy.retentionBackups: Backups: [period]; after that, deleted data is gone from them too.
privacy.rightsIntro: You can use these rights at any time, free of charge. Most of them work directly in the app:
privacy.rightAccess: Access and portability: “Download my data” in Settings gives you a copy of your data as JSON files.
privacy.rightRectification: Correction: change your profile and settings yourself, or ask your box about its records.
privacy.rightErasure: Erasure: delete your profile or your whole account in Settings.
privacy.rightConsent: Withdrawing consent: disconnect a device or turn a feature off; this does not affect what was done before.
privacy.rightComplaint: Complaint: you can complain to the data protection authority where you live or work ({authority}).
privacy.ageBody: Palee is for people aged 16 or older, and we ask you to confirm it when you sign up. If we learn that someone younger has an account, we delete it.
privacy.securityBody: Your data travels encrypted, each box sees only its own records, and staff can see only what their role needs.
privacy.changesBody: If we change this policy in a way that matters, we tell you in the app before the change applies.

terms.intro: These terms apply when you use Palee, on the web or in the apps. By creating an account you accept them.
terms.accountBody: You must be 16 or older. Give true details, keep your password to yourself and tell us if someone else uses your account. One email can hold up to three profiles.
terms.boxesBody: Boxes and coaches use Palee to run their business. Your membership, bookings and prices are agreed between you and the box; Palee provides the software and is not a party to that agreement. Boxes and coaches declare that they act as traders, so you keep your consumer rights towards them.
terms.businessBody1: If you use Palee to run a business, this part applies to you as well. You answer for what you upload and for what you tell your members, for your prices, receipts, taxes and licences, and for your members' data as their controller. You give us permission to show your name, your logo and the content you publish where the service needs it, such as on your own website and, if you choose it, in the programme store.
terms.businessBody2: We may restrict, suspend or stop the service for a business that breaks these terms, the law or other people's rights, or that does not pay. We give you the reasons on a durable medium before the restriction takes effect or when it does, and for stopping the service altogether we give 30 days' notice. We may act sooner where the law obliges us to, where there is an urgent risk to people or to the service, or where serious breaches have already happened more than once. Send a complaint about such a decision to our contact address and we answer within a reasonable time.
terms.businessBody3: If someone brings a claim against Palee because of what your business did, because of your content, or because of your relationship with your members, you cover our costs and our loss, as far as the law allows. This does not apply to people using Palee as consumers.
terms.paymentsBody: When you pay a box in Palee, the box's payment provider handles the payment and the box issues the receipt. Refunds and cancellations follow the box's own terms. Training programmes have their own section below.
terms.programmesBody1: A training programme is sold by the box or the coach, the seller, and not by Palee. The seller declares that it acts as a trader, so you keep your consumer rights towards it. The contract for the programme is between you and the seller. Palee provides the software and is not a party to it. The seller answers for the content of the programme, for its description, for the price and the VAT, for the receipt or invoice, and for your consumer rights.
terms.programmesBody2: You pay inside Palee, but into the seller's own account with the seller's own payment provider. Palee never holds the money and takes no commission on a sale today. If that changes, you will see it in the price before you buy, and we tell sellers in advance.
terms.programmesBody3: You pick a start date, from today up to 60 days ahead. The workouts of the programme arrive on your days from that date. Before you buy you see the titles of the first preview days. You keep the version you bought: if the seller changes the programme later, yours stays as it is. A new price or a new refund rule applies only to people who buy after the change.
terms.programmesBody4: If you buy as a consumer and the seller is established in the EU, the EEA or the United Kingdom, you have 14 days from the purchase to withdraw, without giving a reason. If the start date you picked falls inside those 14 days, we ask you to request expressly that the programme starts then. That box is never ticked for you. If you withdraw after such a request, you get the price back less the part already provided, counted as the days passed over all the days of the programme. If the start is after the 14 days, no such request is needed and you get the whole amount back. To withdraw, open your programme and use the withdrawal button; the amount is shown before you confirm.
terms.programmesBody5: On top of the law the seller picks a refund rule: a full refund until the start date, refunds only inside the withdrawal period, or a refund for the days not yet reached. The rule is shown before you buy and is copied onto your purchase. Where the seller's rule gives you more than the law, the rule applies; where it gives you less, the law applies. The seller makes the refund through its own provider. The iOS and Android apps do not sell programmes: you buy them on the web. A programme is general training information, not medical advice, and no particular result is promised. Ask the seller first about anything to do with the programme. If they do not answer, write to us and we will see what we can do as the platform.
terms.contentBody: What you post stays yours. You give us a non-exclusive, royalty-free licence to store it, copy it, adapt it technically and show it where the service needs it, for as long as you keep it posted and for as long as our backups keep a copy. Do not post anything unlawful, offensive or abusive, other people's private data, or content you have no right to post. We may remove content, hide it, limit how far it travels, or suspend an account that breaks these rules. We act diligently, objectively and proportionately, and we take your rights into account, among them your freedom of expression. How reports and decisions work is in the section on reviews and content reports.
terms.reviewsBody1: Only people who have checked in at a box can review it, one review each. Write your own experience. Do not post insults or hate, anyone else's personal data, ads, off-topic text or unlawful content, and do not post a review that is not a real experience. Nobody may write, buy or ask for a review in exchange for anything, for or against a box.
terms.reviewsBody2: Any member who can see a review, and the box itself, can report it with one of six reasons: offensive or abusive, someone's personal data, not a real experience, ads or off-topic, unlawful content, something else. The last two also need a short explanation. Visitors can report a review by email to moderation@palee.app, the address shown in the footer of every box website. You can send a report in your own language, and we confirm that we received it.
terms.reviewsBody3: Only the Palee team decides. A report on its own changes nothing: the review stays visible and keeps counting in the average until we decide. A box can never hide or delete a review of itself, and no number of reports hides a review by itself. A person decides, with no automated decision-making, and we handle every report in a timely, diligent, non-arbitrary and objective way.
terms.reviewsBody4: A decision is one of three: the review stays, it is hidden so that only its author still sees it and it leaves the average, or its text is removed. If we hide or remove it, we send the author a statement of reasons: what changed, which ground we used, whether the basis is the law or these terms, that a person decided, and where to turn, which is moderation@palee.app and the courts. Whoever reported the review hears the outcome. We can show a hidden review again, again with a statement.
terms.reviewsBody5: So that a report cannot be used as a weapon, limits apply: one open report per person and review, and at most ten reports a day about one box. We may stop accepting reports from someone who repeatedly sends manifestly unfounded ones, and suspend an account that misuses the mechanism. The text of a removed review, and the note that came with a report, are kept for six months after the decision and then deleted; the statement of reasons stays. We do not check what people post before they post it and we have no duty to monitor it. Where we find content unlawful or against these terms we can act on it ourselves, with or without a report. For a review of a training programme the seller may hide the review with a reason, which is abuse, personal data, off-topic or ads, and can never edit it or delete it; a hidden review leaves the average. If you think your review was hidden unfairly, write to moderation@palee.app.
terms.healthBody: Palee is not a medical service. Workouts and suggestions are general information: check with a doctor before you start training, and stop if you feel unwell.
terms.aiBody: Some features use AI to read or suggest things. The results can be wrong, so check them before you rely on them.
terms.availabilityBody: We work to keep Palee available and your data safe, but we cannot promise that it will always be free of errors or interruptions.
terms.endingBody: You can delete your account at any time in Settings. We may close an account that seriously or repeatedly breaks these terms, and we tell you why where the law allows.
terms.liabilityBody: Palee is provided as it is. We are not liable for what you agree with a box or with the seller of a programme, for what other people post, for a loss caused by using a feature in a way it was not meant for, or for training itself. As far as the law allows, we are not liable for lost profit, lost data, lost reputation or other indirect loss, and our liability for any claim is limited to what you paid us in the twelve months before the event, or to 100 euro where you paid us nothing. None of this limits our liability for intent, gross negligence, death or personal injury, or anything else the law does not allow us to limit. Nothing in these terms limits your rights as a consumer.
terms.lawBody: These terms are governed by Greek law, and the courts of Athens are competent. If you use Palee as a consumer, you keep the protection of the law of the country you live in and you can go to its courts. You can also use any out-of-court dispute resolution open to you; we are not obliged to use one.
terms.changesBody: If we change these terms in a way that matters, we tell you in the app before the change applies, and if you keep using Palee after that, the change applies to you. We may add features, change them or stop them, set reasonable limits on use, and try new things with some of the people using Palee. We do not take away a feature you pay for without telling you first.

Sms.title: Text messages (SMS)
Sms.intro: For people without the app, or when something is urgent. The app notification always goes first.

Sms.guide_twilio_1: Sign in at console.twilio.com (or create an account) and upgrade it from the trial so it can send to any number.
Sms.guide_twilio_2: On the Console home page, under Account Info, copy the Account SID and the Auth Token.
Sms.guide_twilio_3: In Messaging › Settings › Geo permissions allow Greece (and every country you send to); check that sender names are allowed there.
Sms.guide_twilio_4: Paste both below and save; we test them at once.
Sms.guide_vonage_1: Sign in at dashboard.nexmo.com (or create a Vonage account) and add credit.
Sms.guide_vonage_2: On the dashboard home page copy the API key and the API secret.
Sms.guide_vonage_3: Optional: ask Vonage support to sign delivery reports, then copy the signature secret from Settings.
Sms.guide_vonage_4: Paste them below and save; we test them at once.
Sms.guide_infobip_1: Sign in at portal.infobip.com (or create an account) and add credit.
Sms.guide_infobip_2: Open Developers › API keys and create a key that may send SMS.
Sms.guide_infobip_3: On the same page copy your Base URL (like https://xxxxx.api.infobip.com).
Sms.guide_infobip_4: Paste both below and save; we test them at once.
Sms.guide_yuboto_1: Sign in at octapush.yuboto.com (or create an account) and buy SMS credit.
Sms.guide_yuboto_2: Ask Yuboto to approve your sender name (the one set above).
Sms.guide_yuboto_3: Open My Account › API Integration and copy the OMNI API key exactly as shown there (it is already encoded).
Sms.guide_yuboto_4: Paste it below and save; we test it at once.
Sms.guide_apifon_1: Sign in at apifon.com (or create an account) and add SMS credit.
Sms.guide_apifon_2: In your account create an API token and copy the token and its secret key.
Sms.guide_apifon_3: Register your sender name with Apifon if you have not done so yet.
Sms.guide_apifon_4: Paste both below and save; we test them at once.
Sms.brevoStep1: Sign in at brevo.com (or create a free account).
Sms.brevoStep2: Open SMTP & API › API keys and choose «Generate a new API key».
Sms.brevoStep3: Buy SMS credits for Greece (Transactional SMS) in Brevo.
Sms.brevoStep4: Paste the key below and save; we test it at once.

Sms.smtpStep3: Fill in the details below and save; we send a test at once.
Sms.smtpStep4: Add the DNS records we show you at your domain.

overview.title: Overview
overview.what: The health of the box in one page: box members, newcomers, who left and who may leave.
overview.how: Every figure covers the period you pick and is compared with the period of the same length just before it. The filters narrow every figure on the page.

training.title: Training
training.what: How classes are used: fill, no-shows, cancellations, busy hours and how workouts are finished.
training.how: Counted from bookings and attendance in the period, compared with the period of the same length before it. The filters apply to the whole page.

coaching.title: Coaching
coaching.what: The coaches' work: classes led, athletes followed, programmes done and ratings.
coaching.how: Counted from the classes, coaching and reviews of the period, compared with the period before it. The filters apply to the whole page.

engagement.title: Engagement
engagement.what: How much box members use Palee: weekly active people, challenges, streaks and activity.
engagement.how: Counted from what box members did in the app and at the box in the period, compared with the period before it. Staff actions are left out.

health.title: Health
health.what: Injuries and recovery: how often they happen, how long they last and where.
health.how: Counted from the injury reports of the period, compared with the period before it. The filters apply to the whole page.

finance.title: Finance
finance.what: The money side of the box: monthly recurring revenue, revenue per box member and collections.
finance.how: Counted from subscriptions, invoices and payments of the period, compared with the period before it. The filters apply to the whole page.

active_members.label: Active box members
active_members.what: Box members with an active subscription package.
active_members.how: Counted on the last day of the period.
active_members.change: A fall usually follows expiring packages that were not renewed: check the renewals list.

net_member_change.label: Net change
net_member_change.what: How many box members you gained or lost overall.
net_member_change.how: Active box members at the end of the period minus those the day before it started.
net_member_change.change: Below zero means more people left than joined: look at churn and new box members together.

new_members.label: New box members
new_members.what: People who took their first subscription package in the period.
new_members.how: Counted by the start of each person's first non-trial package.
new_members.change: A drop often follows fewer trial classes or fewer trials that convert.

churn_rate.label: Churn
churn_rate.what: The share of box members who left during the period.
churn_rate.how: Active the day before the period and without an active package at its end, divided by all active the day before.
churn_rate.change: If it rises, contact the box members at risk and check what changed (schedule, prices, coaches).

trial_conversion.label: Trial conversion
trial_conversion.what: How many trial visitors became box members.
trial_conversion.how: Trial requests of the period that were later converted, divided by all trial requests of the period.
trial_conversion.change: If it falls, follow up sooner after the trial class and check the offer you give.

members_at_risk.label: Box members at risk
members_at_risk.what: Box members Palee sees as likely to leave.
members_at_risk.how: Medium or high retention risk on the period's last day, without the ones you snoozed.
members_at_risk.change: A rise is a call to act: message them or invite them to a class.

class_fill_rate.label: Class fill
class_fill_rate.how: Approved bookings divided by the capacity of the classes in the period (classes without a capacity are left out).
class_fill_rate.change: Low fill on certain hours may mean too many classes at that time; high fill means people may not find a place.

no_show_rate.label: No-shows
no_show_rate.what: Bookings where the person did not come.
no_show_rate.how: Missed attendances divided by missed plus attended ones.
no_show_rate.change: If it rises, remind people before class or review the late cancellation rule.

late_cancellations.label: Late cancellations
late_cancellations.what: Bookings cancelled after the late cancellation time.
late_cancellations.how: Counted from the attendance records of the period.
late_cancellations.change: Many late cancellations take places from others: check the cancellation time and reminders.

waitlist_conversion.label: From the waitlist
waitlist_conversion.what: How many people on a waitlist finally got a place.
waitlist_conversion.how: Waitlisted bookings that were approved, divided by all waitlisted bookings.
waitlist_conversion.change: If it is low, those classes are too small for the demand: consider another class at that time.

visits_per_member_week.label: Visits per week
visits_per_member_week.what: How often a person who trains comes, on average.
visits_per_member_week.how: Attended classes divided by the people who attended and by the weeks of the period.
visits_per_member_week.change: A fall is an early sign of lower motivation, often before people leave.

attendance_by_hour.label: Attendance by hour
attendance_by_hour.what: When people come to class, by hour of the day.
attendance_by_hour.how: Attended classes by the start hour, in the box's time.
attendance_by_hour.change: Move or add classes towards the busy hours.

attendance_by_weekday.label: Attendance by day
attendance_by_weekday.what: Which days people come to class.
attendance_by_weekday.how: Attended classes by the day of the week, in the box's time.
attendance_by_weekday.change: Busy days may need more classes; quiet days may need fewer.

execution_kpis.label: Workout execution
execution_kpis.what: How athletes run their workouts in the app: what they finish, skip, pause and stop.
execution_kpis.how: From the workout executions started in the period.
execution_kpis.change: If completion falls, look at where people stop below and simplify those parts.

classes_per_coach.label: Classes per coach
classes_per_coach.what: How many classes each coach led and how many people attended them.
classes_per_coach.how: Classes of the period by their coach, with the attended places.
classes_per_coach.change: A big gap between coaches may need a fairer schedule.

athletes_per_coach.label: Athletes per coach
athletes_per_coach.what: How many athletes each coach follows personally.
athletes_per_coach.how: Active coaching relationships on the period's last day; the figure is the average per coach.
athletes_per_coach.change: A coach with many more athletes may need help or a limit.

programme_adherence.label: Programme adherence
programme_adherence.what: How many assigned workouts athletes actually did.
programme_adherence.how: Assigned workouts finished from a day before to seven days after their date, divided by all assigned ones up to today.
programme_adherence.change: If it falls, check with the athletes whether the programme suits them.

review_rating_per_coach.label: Ratings per coach
review_rating_per_coach.what: The average class rating per coach.
review_rating_per_coach.how: Reviews of the period by the coach of the class; the figure is the average of all reviews.
review_rating_per_coach.change: Read the low reviews of a coach together with them.

weekly_active_users.label: Active per week
weekly_active_users.what: People who used the app or came to class, per week.
weekly_active_users.how: Different people each week, averaged over the weeks of the period. Staff are left out.
weekly_active_users.change: A fall is often the first sign of lower interest.

challenge_participation.label: Challenge participation
challenge_participation.what: The share of box members who took part in a challenge.
challenge_participation.how: People with progress in a challenge of the period, divided by the active box members.
challenge_participation.change: If it is low, make challenges simpler or announce them better.

booking_streaks.label: Booking streaks
booking_streaks.what: People who train week after week.
booking_streaks.how: People with 4 or more weeks in a row with a class, up to the end of the period.
booking_streaks.change: More long streaks mean steadier habits; a fall needs reminders.

event_mix.label: Activity mix
event_mix.what: What people did in Palee, by kind of activity.
event_mix.how: The recorded events of the period, grouped by category.
event_mix.change: Compare kinds: a rise in one may come from a new feature or a campaign.

injuries_per_1000_attendances.label: Injuries per 1,000 visits
injuries_per_1000_attendances.what: How often injuries happen compared with how much people train.
injuries_per_1000_attendances.how: Injuries reported in the period for every 1,000 attended classes.
injuries_per_1000_attendances.change: If it rises, look at the body areas below and the programming of those weeks.

mean_recovery_days.label: Recovery time
mean_recovery_days.what: How long an injury lasts, on average.
mean_recovery_days.how: Days from start to healing, for the injuries that healed in the period.
mean_recovery_days.change: Longer recoveries may need closer follow-up from the coaches.

top_body_areas.label: Body areas
top_body_areas.how: Injuries of the period by body area.
top_body_areas.change: One area rising may point to an exercise or technique to work on.

mrr.label: Monthly recurring revenue
mrr.what: What the active subscriptions bring in per month.
mrr.how: The price of every active recurring subscription on the period's last day, turned into a monthly amount.
mrr.change: A fall comes from cancelled or cheaper subscriptions: compare with churn.

arpm.label: Revenue per box member
arpm.what: What a box member brings in per month, on average.
arpm.how: Paid revenue of the period divided by the active box members and by the months of the period.
arpm.change: A rise means better packages or extras; a fall may mean more discounts.

ltv.label: Lifetime value
ltv.what: An estimate of what a box member brings in over the whole time they stay.
ltv.how: Revenue per box member divided by the monthly churn. Empty when nobody left.
ltv.change: It moves with churn: keeping people longer raises it the most.

on_time_collection.label: Paid on time
on_time_collection.what: The share of invoices paid by their due date.
on_time_collection.how: Invoices due in the period and paid in full by the due date, divided by all invoices due in the period.
on_time_collection.change: If it falls, send reminders before the due date.

days_sales_outstanding.label: Days to get paid
days_sales_outstanding.what: How long an invoice waits to be paid, on average.
days_sales_outstanding.how: Days from issue to the last payment, for invoices paid in full in the period.
days_sales_outstanding.change: If it grows, ask for payment at the desk or turn on online payment.

revenue_per_package.label: Revenue per subscription package
revenue_per_package.what: Which subscription packages bring in the money.
revenue_per_package.how: Paid revenue of the period by subscription package, minus refunds.
revenue_per_package.change: Promote the packages that work and review the ones that bring little.

age_bands.label: Age
age_bands.what: The ages of the box members who chose to share them.
age_bands.how: Active box members by the age they gave for the leaderboards. Groups of fewer than 5 people are hidden.
age_bands.change: Use it to shape classes and messages for the groups you have.

genders.label: Gender
genders.what: The gender of the box members who chose to share it.
genders.how: Active box members by the division they chose for the leaderboards. Groups of fewer than 5 people are hidden.
genders.change: Use it to see who your classes reach.

paid_revenue.what: Money actually paid in the period.
paid_revenue.change: Open Finance to see which payments are missing.

reviews.what: Reviews box members left in the period.
reviews.change: Many reviews at once usually follow a change: read the newest ones.

active_injuries.what: Injuries that are not healed yet.
active_injuries.change: Open Health to see who needs a scaled programme.

notification_clicks.what: Times people opened a notification from the box.
notification_clicks.change: Few clicks mean the messages are not useful enough: try fewer and clearer ones.

operational_status.what: A few things that need attention: finance, low ratings, expiring memberships and coaching.
operational_status.change: Each line is a task: open the page it belongs to.

team_completions.what: Team workouts finished in the period.
team_completions.change: More team workouts usually mean a stronger community.

individual_completions.what: Workouts finished alone in the period.
individual_completions.change: Compare with team workouts to see how people like to train.

total_completions.what: All workouts finished in the period, team and alone.
total_completions.change: A fall here often comes before a fall in attendance.

attendance_status.what: Attendance records by what happened: attended, missed, cancelled.
attendance_status.change: Many missed or late-cancelled places need reminders.

push_delivery.what: App notifications by what happened to them: sent, failed and so on.
push_delivery.change: Many failures may mean old devices: ask people to open the app again.

communication.what: Messages between the box and box members, by direction.
communication.change: Many messages to the box may point to a question you can answer once for everyone.

active_athletes.what: Athletes with personal coaching right now.
active_athletes.change: Compare with the coaches you have to see how full they are.

captured_events.what: Coaching actions recorded in the period.
captured_events.change: Few actions may mean athletes are not followed closely.

reviews.what: Reviews of coaching in the period.
reviews.change: Read them with the coach they are about.

active_injuries.what: Injuries reported and not healed yet.
active_injuries.change: Check that each one has a scaled programme.

total_reports.what: All injury reports of the period, healed or not.
total_reports.change: Compare with the injuries per 1,000 visits to see if more training explains it.

recent_injury_flags.change: Talk to the athletes flagged before their next workout.

completion_rate.change: If it falls, see below where people stop.

score_capture.change: Remind people to log their score at the end.

skip_rate.change: Many skips may mean the countdowns are too long.

time_to_start.change: A long wait may mean the workout is hard to read before starting.

pauses.change: Many pauses may mean the workout is too long or hard.

review_drop_off.change: Make the finish steps shorter if many stop there.

median_duration.change: Compare with the time you planned for the workout.

clock_adjusted.change: Many adjustments may mean the planned times are wrong.

abandon_by_format.change: Simplify the formats where most people stop.

abandon_points.change: Look at these parts: they may be too long or unclear.

free_text.change: If free text workouts stop early, write them as structured ones.

daily_trend.what: Workouts started each day, finished or not.
daily_trend.change: Quiet days may follow the schedule or the programming.

completion_by_format.what: How often workouts are finished, by format (AMRAP, EMOM…).
completion_by_format.change: A format with low completion may need a shorter time.

completion_by_source.what: How often workouts are finished, by where they came from (class, coach, own choice).
completion_by_source.change: Compare sources to see which workouts people stick with.

structured.what: Workouts written step by step, started and finished.
structured.change: Compare with free text workouts to see which kind people finish.

retirement.change: Many stops in one Flow may mean its clock is too long for your members.

active_memberships.change: A fall usually means renewals were missed.

expiring.what: Memberships that end in the next 30 days.
expiring.change: Contact these people before the end to renew.

revenue.change: Compare with the pending invoices to see what is still to come.

credit_balance.what: Credit box members have with the box, still unused.
credit_balance.change: A large balance is money you owe in classes or products.

pending_invoices.what: Invoices not yet paid in full.
pending_invoices.change: Ask for payment at the desk or with a reminder.

overdue_invoices.what: Unpaid invoices past their due date.

renewal_rate.what: The share of memberships renewed when they ended.
renewal_rate.change: If it falls, contact people before their membership ends.

credit_offsets.what: Invoice amounts covered by credit instead of money.
credit_offsets.change: Many offsets lower the cash you collect.

monthly_revenue.what: Revenue per month: paid and still pending.
monthly_revenue.how: Payments and open invoices grouped by month.
monthly_revenue.change: A growing pending line means payments are late.

revenue_streams.what: Where the revenue comes from: subscriptions, products, events and more.
revenue_streams.change: Grow the streams that work best.

expiring_soon.what: The people whose membership ends soon.

overdue_list.what: Invoices past their due date, with the days overdue.

pending_payments.change: Confirm or reject them so the figures stay right.

pending_rewards.what: Referral rewards waiting to be given.
pending_rewards.change: Give them soon, so people keep inviting friends.

history.title: Reset history

ClassTypeOptions.event_tip: Bookings use the package's event visits, not its class visits.
ClassTypeOptions.event_what: A booking in a class of this type takes event visits from the member's subscription package. Their class visits stay untouched.
ClassTypeOptions.event_members: Only members whose package includes events can book. On the schedule the class carries an «Event» tag, and the «Events» filter finds it.
ClassTypeOptions.event_when: For anything that is not everyday training: a seminar, workshop, open day or in-house competition. If every subscription should cover the class, leave it a regular class.
ClassTypeOptions.visits_tip: How many package visits one booking uses. Usually 1.
ClassTypeOptions.visits_what: Each booking takes this many visits from the member's package, from 1 to 10. A longer or costlier class can cost more without a separate package.
ClassTypeOptions.visits_members: Before booking, members see how many visits the class uses. With an 8-visit package and a 2-visit class, they can book it 4 times.
ClassTypeOptions.visits_when: For classes that cost you more: small groups, 90-minute sessions, special equipment or a guest coach. Regular classes stay at 1.
ClassTypeOptions.level_tip: Which levels the class suits. With none chosen, all levels.
ClassTypeOptions.level_what: Pick one or more: Beginners, Intermediate, Advanced. With none chosen the class is for all levels. It informs; it never blocks a booking.
ClassTypeOptions.level_members: The level shows in the class details. Anyone who filters the schedule, the box page or «Around me» by «Beginners» finds the classes for beginners and those for all levels.
ClassTypeOptions.level_when: Mark the classes a newcomer should not pick by chance (Olympic lifting for Advanced only) and those that make the best first visit (Foundations for Beginners). A class scaled for everyone stays with none chosen.
ClassTypeOptions.audience_tip: Which groups the class is made for. With none chosen, everyone.
ClassTypeOptions.audience_what: Pick the groups the class is built for, such as «Teens». With none chosen it is for everyone. This also informs; it never blocks a booking.
ClassTypeOptions.audience_members: The groups show in the class details, and members filter the schedule and the box page by them.
ClassTypeOptions.audience_when: When the class is designed for particular people: women only, kids, over 40. Open classes stay with none chosen, so nobody thinks they are not for them.
